concerns.concern: The test showing equal signals in two orthogonal geometries cannot tell the spin Seebeck effect apart from an anomalous Nernst effect. In a randomly oriented composite, averaging over interfaces gives the same symmetry as an ANE, so an isotropic ANE source would also give equal coefficients.
concerns.quote: Isotropy is a necessary consequence of the microstructure, not a signature of the SSE.

concerns.concern: There are no decisive control experiments establishing the SSE origin. Missing are a Pt-coated non-magnetic garnet (GGG/YAG), a sign-reversal test with W or Ta, and temperature-dependence or high-field magnon-suppression measurements.
concerns.quote: Without at least one of these, "observed signals originate purely from the SSE of YIG" is an overstatement.

concerns.concern: Effective conductivity alone is not a performance metric. The composites' spin Seebeck coefficients are one to two orders of magnitude below YIG/Pt references, so their power factor is within or below the thin-film range, and no side-by-side power-factor comparison is given.
concerns.quote: The headline "2–3 orders of magnitude higher σ^eff" therefore risks misleading readers about the practical gain.

concerns.concern: The effective-conductivity benchmark depends mainly on the arbitrary substrate or ferromagnet thickness of the reference devices. Thinned-film or multilayer references with ferromagnet thickness near the magnon length would give comparable values, and such references are absent.
concerns.quote: So the comparison mostly reflects the choice of reference devices rather than an intrinsic advantage.

concerns.concern: The 'trans-scale/volumetric' mechanism is asserted but not modeled. No effective-medium or network model links the composite response to known YIG/Pt interface parameters, so the low spin Seebeck coefficient remains unexplained.
concerns.quote: No effective-medium or network model predicts S_SSE and σ^eff of the composite from thin-film YIG/Pt parameters

concerns.concern: No experiment varies the YIG particle size relative to the magnon diffusion length, which would be the defining test of the trans-scale concept. The illustrative figure of volumetric conversion is only a cartoon.
concerns.quote: No experiment varies YIG particle size relative to λm (~10 µm), which would be the defining test of the "trans-scale" concept.

concerns.concern: The field dependence in the in-plane-field geometry keeps rising up to 5–7 kOe, although magnetization saturates by 1–2 kOe. This non-saturating component is not identified, separated or demagnetization-corrected, so the near-identical coefficients in the two geometries may be partly coincidental.
concerns.quote: The non-saturating component (e.g., ordinary Nernst of the Pt network, or an unidentified phase) is not identified, separated, or demagnetization-corrected.

concerns.concern: Excluding secondary magnetic phases by XRD is not quantitative. XRD has 1–5 wt% detection limits and would miss nanometric or amorphous interfacial phases, for example from Pt–Fe interdiffusion.
concerns.quote: XRD has detection limits of ~1–5 wt%. Nanometric or amorphous interfacial phases ... would be invisible.

concerns.concern: The magnetization-decrease argument cannot exclude a small ferromagnetic fraction unless the expected dilution from the actual Pt mass fraction is computed and compared.
concerns.quote: The expected dilution from the actual Pt mass fraction must be computed and compared.

concerns.concern: The quoted YIG saturation magnetization is the 0 K value rather than the room-temperature value. The plotted magnetization values appear three orders of magnitude off, indicating a units or normalization error that undermines the magnetization argument.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3f plots values of ~0.02–0.03 "emu/g", which is three orders of magnitude off and must be a units or normalization error.

concerns.concern: The Hall measurement used to exclude anomalous Hall/ANE contributions is noisy. Its detection limit is not converted into an upper bound on a possible ANE contribution.
concerns.quote: The Hall test is noisy (±~100 nV at 100 mA), and no detection limit is converted into an upper bound on a possible ANE contribution.

concerns.concern: The Pt-thickness and processing trends are interpreted superficially. The SSE current scales about ×4 with Pt thickness, which does not fit interface-driven SSE. The invoked spin-diffusion-length dependence is also quantitatively inconsistent with the data.
concerns.quote: The authors instead invoke the "typical λs dependence", which is not quantitatively consistent

concerns.concern: Reproducibility is not shown. There is one sample per condition from a single batch, the isotropy test is done on only one sample, and there are no sample-to-sample error bars.
concerns.quote: One sample per condition, all from a single batch.

concerns.concern: Thermal gradients are inferred from thermocouples across the heat baths, including interface drops, and the two geometries use different contact schemes. This introduces unquantified systematic errors. No heat-flux-normalized coefficients or on-sample thermography are provided.
concerns.quote: absolute S_SSE values, and especially their cross-geometry agreement, carry unquantified systematic errors.

concerns.concern: zT and power density per volume are not reported, yet they are needed to support the claim of bridging spin caloritronics with macroscopic devices.
concerns.quote: zT (≈10⁻¹⁰ from the reported κ) and power density per volume are not reported.

concerns.concern: Novelty is limited because bulk nanocomposite and sintered polycrystalline SSE systems have already been reported (Boona et al., Lee et al., Uchida et al.).
concerns.quote: The bulk-nanocomposite SSE concept is not new.

concerns.concern: Demonstrated performance is very low (zT ~10⁻¹⁰), and the work reads as a processing demonstration rather than a physics advance at top-tier level. The discussion should acknowledge this and give a quantitative roadmap.
concerns.quote: In its current form the work reads as a materials-processing demonstration more than a physics advance at the level expected by a top-tier journal.

concerns.concern: The 15 and 30 nm Pt thicknesses are nominal, extrapolated from deposition time. No Pt mass fraction measurement (ICP/EDX) or post-sintering TEM is reported to confirm thickness distribution and continuity.
concerns.quote: The 15/30-nm Pt thicknesses are nominal, extrapolated from deposition time on the 5-nm sample.

concerns.concern: Uniaxial pressing likely produces anisotropic Pt channels. The manuscript does not state the pressing-axis orientation relative to the temperature gradient or to the conductivity measurement direction.
concerns.quote: Uniaxial pressing likely creates anisotropic Pt channels. The manuscript does not state which geometry has ∇T or the σ^eff measurement direction along the pressing axis

concerns.concern: The description of 'micrometer-scale Pt channels' formed from 15–30 nm coatings is unclear.
concerns.quote: "Micrometer-scale Pt channels" from 15–30-nm coatings is unclear and needs clarification.

concerns.concern: The language is overstated, for example claiming the signal is 'purely' SSE or that the results 'rigorously validate' the conclusions.
concerns.quote: Moderate overstated language such as "purely", "rigorously validate", and "clearly demonstrating".

concerns.concern: A figure cross-reference is wrong: the text says Fig. 3e agrees with 'Hx-∇zT (Fig. 3c)', which should read Hz-∇xT.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3e is cited as Hx-∇zT, but the text says it agrees with "Hx-∇zT (Fig. 3c)"; this should read Hz-∇xT.

concerns.concern: The same PDF card number is assigned to both Y₂O₃ and FePt.
concerns.quote: The same PDF card #43-0661 is assigned to both Y₂O₃ and FePt.

concerns.concern: The Cu-Kα wavelength is given inconsistently between the Methods and the Supplementary Note.
concerns.quote: Cu-Kα is given as 0.15406 nm in Methods but 0.15418 nm in Note S2.

concerns.concern: Supplementary Note S2 cites the wrong supplementary figure for the XRD data.
concerns.quote: Note S2 refers to "Fig. S2" for XRD; this should be Fig. S3.

concerns.concern: The author contributions list VSM for magnetometry, while the Methods state SQUID-MPMS.
concerns.quote: Author contributions list VSM, whereas Methods state SQUID-MPMS.

concerns.concern: There are typographical errors in the text, including a misspelled name and a wrong word.
concerns.quote: "Galosov" (Golosov) and "It is worth nothing" are typos.

concerns.concern: The Fig. S4 caption mentions dashed lines only in panels (b)–(c), although they also appear in panels (d)–(e).
concerns.quote: The Fig. S4 caption describes dashed lines only in panels (b)–(c), though they also appear in (d)–(e).
